spoken_text: Sell one billion rupiah of BCA stock on the Jakarta exchange, and your final tax is 0.1%, or one million rupiah. Done. Sell that exact same gain on Apple or the S&P 500 from Jakarta, and Indonesia's worldwide tax rules kick in. Under the HPP Law, offshore capital gains are ordinary income, taxed progressively up to 35%. That is a 350-times tax shock.

spoken_text: Most Indonesian investors open Interactive Brokers, Pluang, or Gotrade to buy US shares. Filing Form W-8BEN cuts US dividend withholding from 30% down to 15%, creditable back home through PPh 24. But here is the trap: the US Estate Tax. If you are not an American citizen, the IRS gives you an exemption of just sixty thousand dollars. Above that, the IRS seizes up to 40% upon death. Indonesia has zero estate tax treaty with the United States.

If you're not an American citizen, the I.R.S. gives you an exemption of just sixty thousand dollars. Above that, the I.R.S. takes up to forty percent upon death. And Indonesia has zero estate tax treaty with the U.S.

spoken_text: Smart investors bypass both traps using Irish-domiciled UCITS ETFs on the London Stock Exchange, like CSPX for the S&P 500, or VWRA for global equities. First, Ireland's US treaty caps internal dividend withholding at 15%, while charging 0% outbound withholding to you. Second, Irish funds are non-US situs assets. The 40% US estate tax drops to zero. Best of all, accumulating shares reinvest dividends inside the fund, triggering zero annual dividend tax events.

spoken_text: What if you receive cash dividends from abroad? By default, Indonesia taxes foreign dividends as ordinary income up to 35%. Here is the legal escape hatch. Under the Omnibus Law and PMK 18 of 2021, foreign dividends are 100% tax-exempt if you repatriate and reinvest them in Indonesia before March 31. Lock the money into Indonesian government SBN bonds, mutual funds, or deposits for three consecutive years, and your tax rate drops to zero.
tts_transcript: What if you receive cash dividends from abroad? By default, Indonesia taxes foreign dividends as ordinary income... up to thirty-five percent. Here's the legal escape hatch. Under the Omnibus Law and P.M.K. eighteen, twenty twenty-one, foreign dividends are one hundred percent tax-exempt if you repatriate and re-invest them in Indonesia before March thirty-first. Lock the money into Indonesian government S.B.N. bonds, mutual funds, or deposits for three consecutive years... and your tax rate drops to zero.

spoken_text: Can you hide behind a Singapore holding company or a BVI paper shell? Do not try it. Under PMK 93 of 2019, Controlled Foreign Corporation rules treat passive gains in offshore entities you control as deemed dividends, taxing them anyway. Worse, bank secrecy is dead. Under the CRS global agreement, over one hundred countries, including Singapore and Switzerland, automatically report your account balances to the DJP every September. Unreported offshore assets risk penalties up to 200%.

spoken_text: Here is your three-tier playbook. One: under sixty thousand dollars, direct US stocks with Form W-8BEN are acceptable. Two: above sixty thousand dollars, switch entirely to Irish accumulating UCITS ETFs like CSPX and VWRA. You eliminate the 40% US estate tax, stop dividend drag, and report your acquisition cost in your annual SPT tax return. Three: for cash dividends, repatriate into Indonesian SBN bonds for three years under PMK 18 to lock in 0% tax. Structure properly, and keep your gains.
